fixes.explanation: Three men from each tribe, just like Joshua says (Joshua 18:4). Three is the number, friend. I bet those men wore out a lot of sandals before the job was done. The text says they went throughout the land, mapping it city by city into seven portions (Joshua 18:9).

Gilgal sounds like a solid guess, friend, but the Tent doesn't go up there this time. The text says the whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting there (Joshua 18:1). I've done the same thing. I once searched the top shelf for a cookie box that was sitting on the counter the whole time, and I was LOUD about how sure I was.

Altars are holy business, friend, but nobody hands out altar duty in this plan. Joshua sends the men out to "…survey the land and map it out…" (Joshua 18:4). Their whole assignment is the map. Picture showing up to the job with a truck full of stones when the boss asked for a clipboard.

Emptying isn't in the verse, friend. The text says Joshua "…rebuilt the city and settled in it." (Joshua 19:50). Rebuilding is building up, not clearing out. Emptying a place and then moving in sounds like me scrubbing the whole oven spotless and settling down with zero cookies. Nobody's happy in that kitchen.
